content.title: The Marathon World Record & Fastest Marathon Times [Updated April 2026]
content.text: Here’s all you need to know about the marathon world record and the world’s fastest marathon times runners. We’ve got lists of the out-right fastest marathons, including multiple times by the same runners, plus we list the 10 fastest men and women to have ever run a marathon. Last update: 20 April 2026 What Is The Marathon World Record? The current men’s marathon world record is 2:00:35 by Kelvin Kiptum (Kenya). The current women’s marathon world record is 2:09:56 by Ruth Chepngetich (Kenya). In this article we’re looking at the following times (you can click the links below to jump to the tables). The London Marathon is a course which qualifies for a women’s only record. The women’s only world record is 2:15:50 run by Tigst Assefa at the 2025 London Marathon. Boston Marathon is not a record-eligible course because it’s a point-to-point course and World Athletics rules state that ‘the start and finish points on the course, measured along a straight line between them, shall not be further apart than 50% of the race distance.’ It also has a net downhill which is beyond the limit allowed by World Athletics. FAQ About The Fastest Marathon Runners Who is the best marathon runner in the world right now?Based on current performances, Kenya’s Sabastian Sawe and John Korir, plus Uganda’s Jacob Kiplimo, are the best men’s marathon runners. The best women’s marathon runners include Ethiopia’s Tigst Assefa and the Netherlands’s Sifan Hassan. Both have been incredibly consistent and successful in recent years. What is a good marathon time?For amateur runners, many have the initial aim of running under four hours in a marathon. Sub-three is the goal of faster and more competitive runners. What is the fastest marathon in the world?Both the men’s and women’s world records were run at the Chicago Marathon but there are several other very quick marathon courses including the London Marathon, Berlin Marathon and Valencia Marathon.
